title: Gaussian residual-link evidence was sensitive to mouse removal in 82 selected Allen slice connections
abstract: We tested whether first-to-third response links after removal of the middle response exceed Gaussian sampling noise in selected Allen mouse visual cortex slices. We reused verified three-pulse sufficient statistics from prior SCI work. A response-independent selection of one connection per inferred mouse gave 82 connections. Fisher combination of exact Gaussian partial-correlation p values gave p = 0.033575. Mean squared partial correlation was 0.047105 versus a null mean of 0.038551. Removing one mouse raised p above 0.05 in seven of 82 checks. A conservative test that used all 255 connections and allowed dependence within mice gave p = 0.182293. Thus the evidence is weak and sensitive to the test. Non-Gaussian trials, response fits, selection and inferred mouse labels limit inference. No biological memory mechanism or held-out prediction gain was established. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, hashes and verified external retrieval steps support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Connection p value counts under the Gaussian zero-partial-correlation model. Dashed lines show uniform-null expected counts. One-per-mouse evidence is sensitive to individual mice.
